Summary: Attached files lost when the page changes
Description: Evidence attached to the create-ticket form was discarded whenever the form re-rendered (e.g. a validation error). TicketAttachment rows were only created inside the success branch, so the uploaded bytes never touched disk.
Expected: Files the analyst already uploaded survive a validation error and are attached to the ticket on the retry.
Resolution: Server-side staging: new StagedAttachment model + apps/incidents/staging.py. Uploads persist BEFORE form validation, are shown back as 'held for you' chips, and are adopted onto the ticket on success. Migration incidents/0054. A browser cannot repopulate a file input after a page load, so only server-side retention can fix this.

Summary: Attaching files from a second folder wipes the first batch
Description: A second trip through the file picker replaced the whole selection instead of adding to it. There was no JavaScript managing file inputs anywhere in the codebase.
Expected: Picks from multiple folders accumulate; the analyst can see and individually remove what is attached.
Resolution: New _evidence_picker.html + _evidence_picker_js.html: a DataTransfer-based accumulating picker with a removable chip list, per-file type/size checks and a running total. Also raised nginx client_max_body_size 26M -> 128M, since an oversized batch was previously rejected with a bare 413 before Django ran.

Summary: Ticket-detail upload only accepted one file at a time
Description: AttachmentForm accepted exactly one file per POST, while most evidence is added after the ticket exists.
Expected: Multiple files can be uploaded in one go, sharing a single description.
Resolution: Added MultipleFileField / MultipleFileInput; upload_attachment now loops the cleaned list. Invalid files are named individually rather than a generic error.

Summary: System Admin can view and export the incident report
Description: Report access was governed entirely by Ticket.objects.visible_to() with no report-specific permission, and the three report buttons were completely ungated. Exporting also WROTE to the ticket (report_generated_by / report_sha256 / stale-report watermark), so a party to the incident could overwrite the SOC's provenance record.
Expected: The incident report is a SOC deliverable. Roles that merely appear in a case should not be able to mint or regenerate it.
Resolution: New _can_access_ticket_report(): SOC + superuser only, raising 404. System Admin, System Owner, Forensic and Red Team Manager all lost preview/DOCX/PDF. Buttons gated via a can_access_report flag; stale-report badge gated too. Their other controls (containment form, attachments, transitions) are untouched.

Summary: Section 8 of the Incident Report carries an unnecessary checklist
Description: Section 8 printed a fixed 15-item remediation checklist that was static boilerplate: always rendered unticked and driven by no ticket field. Section 6 already carries a real data-driven containment checklist.
Expected: Section 8 shows only its two real data rows (Investigation Findings, Countermeasure).
Resolution: Removed REMEDIATION_CHECKLIST from report_content.py, reports.py, the HTML/PDF template and the DOCX builder. Template rebuilt and verified: all 15 items gone, zero ballot-box glyphs. Added a test asserting the committed .docx no longer contains the strings, since the existing test compares only {{placeholders}} and would miss a stale rebuild.

Summary: Incident Report should match the NT paper form layout
Description: Comparison against a filled INC-2026-00019 form showed differences in banner text, row numbering, checkbox ordering, date format and a missing IoC row.
Expected: Report visually aligns with the NT form the SOC files alongside it.
Resolution: Banner -> 'INCIDENT REPORT: Containment'; section 1 rows numbered 1.1-1.20; checkbox options reordered low->high; Thai Buddhist dates (2 / ก.ค. / 69 11:00 น.) on the section-1 date rows only; new Ticket.ioc_user field + 'User' row in section 4 (migration 0055); Hardening contact added to the coordination note; fixed a pre-existing DOCX/PDF drift where the 'ข้อ ๑' appendix heading was missing from HTML. NOTE: section-1 numbers run over our wider row set, so they deliberately do NOT correspond one-for-one with the NT form's 1.1-1.18.

Summary: Anyone can delete attached files with no confirmation
Description: Deletion was one click with no confirmation. Any SOC member could delete any attachment on any ticket, including on a CLOSED/APPROVED case, and the create-form staged chip hard-deleted the file with no audit at all. The soft delete had no restore path in the product.
Expected: Evidence removal is deliberate, attributable, reversible, and impossible once a case is closed.
Resolution: Narrowed to uploader + SOC Manager; added the TERMINAL_STATUSES gate every other evidence action already had; mandatory reason stored on deleted_reason and in the TicketLog note; confirmation modal; staged discard became recoverable with an undo; SOC-Manager restore UI. Also versioned timeline-note edits (TicketLogRevision + 'แก้ไขแล้ว' badge) because a deletion's only audit trace could previously be rewritten by the person who deleted it. Migration incidents/0056.

Summary: Decisions cannot be undone and submitted content cannot be edited
Description: Four decisions were genuinely one-way: closure, the SOC Manager's forward at PENDING_MGR_TRIAGE, Tier 2's reclassify-to-Event close, and manager approval. Separately there was NO ticket edit view at all, so Tier 1 content could only ever be corrected by Tier 2 during ESCALATED_T2. Where editing existed it was destructive (containment reports overwritten, subtask result notes overwritten with no log).
Expected: Mistakes can be corrected with an audit trail; closed cases stay closed.
Resolution: Three phases. (1) TicketFieldChange + apps/incidents/history.py recording field/old/new/author, hooked into Tier 2 review, containment resubmit and subtask notes. (2) edit_ticket view + TicketEditForm - creator while NEW, SOC after, closed frozen; cannot change status or route. (3) Ticket.step_back() - SOC Manager only, mandatory reason, PENDING_MANAGER resolves its target from t1_route. APPROVED and CLOSED_EVENT remain terminal. Migration incidents/0057.

Summary: CSP test is stricter than CSP requires
Description: test_no_inline_script_on_the_page_is_missing_a_nonce rejects ANY nonce-less <script>, including Django's json_script data blocks, which are inert and never executed. The two existing json_script calls at ticket_detail.html:401-402 only pass because they render inside a conditional the test's ticket does not hit.
Expected: Decide whether json_script data blocks should be exempt from the nonce assertion.
Resolution: Worked around by hand-serialising the attachment limits with a private escape table. Worth resolving deliberately rather than leaving a 7th, different mechanism for handing data to scripts.

Summary: Batch size cap not enforced on ticket-detail uploads
Description: MAX_ATTACHMENT_BATCH_SIZE is enforced in stage_uploads (create flow) but MultipleFileField.clean checks per-file rules only. The picker advertises the cap identically on all three pages, so on ticket detail it is client-side only and bypassable with JS disabled.
Expected: All three upload surfaces enforce the same batch rule server-side.
Resolution: Not fixed: closing it changes behaviour (detail-page uploads would start being capped), so it needs a decision rather than a silent refactor. Suggested fix is a shared validate_attachment_batch() in models.py beside validate_attachment.

Description: Ticket.step_back() deliberately bypasses ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS and hand-rolls its own status write plus log entry, so every invariant transition_to() maintains must be remembered twice. This already caused one bug: status_changed_at was not being stamped, so stepped-back tickets showed their original queue age and sorted wrongly.
Expected: Backward moves go through the same machinery as forward ones.
Resolution: Symptom fixed (step_back now stamps status_changed_at and clears the T2 claim). The structural fix - adding these edges to ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS with a MANAGER_STEP_BACK permission token and reducing step_back to a transition_to call - is a state-machine redesign and was left for a scheduled piece of work. This is the one I would actively recommend scheduling.
